text: Petrolimex and Japan's ENEOS deepen strategic partnership with new MoU

HÀ NỘI The Vietnam National Petroleum Group (Petrolimex) and ENEOS Corporation on November 9 exchanged a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) under the witness of General Secretary and President Tô Lâm and Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae during the official visit to Japan by the Vietnamese top leader.
Building on a strategic partnership established in 2016, the MoU marks a new milestone in cooperation between the two corporations.

The agreement focuses on strengthening and diversifying petroleum supply sources, enhancing resilience against supply chain disruptions, and exploring opportunities for collaboration in high-quality petroleum products, petrochemicals, and new energy solutions.
For Petrolimex, cooperation with ENEOS reflects a proactive approach to preparing for Việt Nam's long-term energy needs.

At a time when global energy markets remain subject to significant uncertainties, expanding international sourcing options is an important step in enhancing the Group's adaptability and fulfilling its responsibility to ensure adequate fuel supplies for the national economy.
As Việt Nam's largest downstream petroleum enterprise, Petrolimex operates an extensive infrastructure network and nationwide distribution system.
The Group's supply capabilities play a vital role in meeting fuel demand for production, business activities, and everyday life across the country.
Partnering with Petrolimex is one of Japan's leading energy companies.
According to ENEOS, as of March 31, 2026, the company operated nine refineries with a combined crude oil processing capacity of approximately 1.64 million barrels per day.
ENEOS also operated more than 11,000 service stations across Japan and held around 50% of the country's petroleum products market during fiscal year 2025.

The significance of this partnership lies in the combination of ENEOS's supply capabilities, technological expertise, and operational experience with Petrolimex's infrastructure, distribution network, and deep understanding of the Vietnamese market.
Leveraging these complementary strengths, the two companies will explore long-term business opportunities tailored to Việt Nam's short- and long-term energy needs.

For Petrolimex, partnering with an industry-leading company creates opportunities to strengthen sourcing capabilities, improve service quality, and gain further experience in operating according to international standards.

Importantly, in the event of unexpected market disruptions or supply shortages, Petrolimex and ENEOS will implement appropriate cooperation measures, including sourcing alternative supplies and coordinating logistics solutions.
Specific supply and trading arrangements will be governed through separate agreements.
This framework will enable Petrolimex to broaden its sourcing options, enhance procurement flexibility, and strengthen supply chain management.

After a decade of collaboration, further deepening relations with ENEOS demonstrates Petrolimex's international partnership capabilities and long-term strategic vision, while reinforcing its role as a key enterprise in ensuring fuel supplies for Việt Nam's socio-economic development.

Beyond supply security, developing opportunities to provide high-quality petroleum products tailored to the increasingly diverse needs of the Vietnamese market is another important area of the Petrolimex-ENEOS partnership.

This direction aligns with Petrolimex's Horizon 2030 strategy, which aims to transform the company into a smart energy, services, and utilities group while increasing the application of technology in business operations and customer service.
In the product segment, the two companies will study opportunities to supply and develop premium-grade gasoline and diesel fuels, Jet A-1 aviation fuel, marine fuels, and specialised fuels.

They will also explore cooperation in biofuels, low-emission fuels, Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF), synthetic fuels, and other new energy products, supporting both evolving customer needs and broader energy transition objectives.
